content: {"summary":"Both kafka-01 and kafka-02 stopped after a config push on 2026-08-13 because the pushed `message.max.bytes=10MB` value was invalid, causing a ConfigException that aborted the JVM. systemd reported the restart as successful because the kafka unit is Type=simple, which marks the service active before the JVM exits.","likely_cause":"Invalid `message.max.bytes` value (10MB) caused Kafka brokers to abort during startup; systemd’s Type=simple unit reported success before the abort.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The config push set `message.max.bytes=10MB`, which Kafka rejects, causing a ConfigException and broker shutdown.","evidence_ids":["INC-0185#0"],"quote":"JVM quit with a `ConfigException` naming `message.max.bytes`."},{"text":"systemd treats the kafka unit as up instantly, so restart returns 0 even though the JVM aborts shortly after.","evidence_ids":["INC-0185#2"],"quote":"restart returns 0 even when the JVM is about to abort"},{"text":"Both kafka-01 and kafka-02 died after the push despite systemctl restart exit code 0.","evidence_ids":["INC-0185#0"],"quote":"same steps on the next broker, with the same result"}],"next_checks":["Verify that byte-valued Kafka settings are plain integers without suffixes before pushing config","Add a lint rule to reject unit suffixes in Kafka config files","Change the kafka systemd unit to a type that reports failure if the process exits quickly (e.g., Type=notify)","Implement health‑check after each broker restart to confirm it rejoined the cluster","Review runbook RB-027 to ensure manual verification of broker status after a push"]}
